facts.fact: ITWeb Africa describes SmartCare Pro and SmartCare 2.0 as the latest versions of Zambia's electronic health record systems, developed by the Ministry of Health and the Smart Zambia Institute; no date is given for this, so the publication date is used.

ITWeb Africa says SmartCare Pro is designed to modernise health infrastructure across more than 2,000 facilities; the figure counts health facilities of every kind, gives no denominator and does not separate primary clinics; undated, so the publication date is used.

At the GovLink private 4G launch at Ndola Teaching Hospital, reported 16 July 2026, government said SmartCare Pro and SmartCare 2.0 will be migrated to the new government-owned network, with three Copperbelt hospitals connected first ahead of a nationwide rollout.

ITWeb Africa describes SmartCare 2.0 as the latest hospital-focused version of the electronic health record platform, with Ndola Teaching Hospital, Kitwe Teaching Hospital and Arthur Davison Children's Hospital the first facilities connected to GovLink; undated beyond the report, so the publication date is used.
